[post-training] Read TaskTrove Clean directly (#9125)

Allow SkyRL experiments to select TaskTrove Clean rows by exact source,
tags,
modes, limit, and seed. The resolved source names one packed Parquet
object,
release identity, and manifest-pinned verifier. MarinSkyRL#549 validates
and
records selection membership before GPU allocation, caches that object
once per
node, and extracts task archives only when a rollout batch constructs
its
Harbor trials. Harbor remains unchanged and receives concrete task
directories.

Replace the smoke's intermediate 2,685-object artifact with a direct
dependency
on `tasktrove/clean`. An rno2a run using Qwen3-0.6B staged one Parquet
file,
completed 16 Harbor trials and one FSDP update, saved `global_step_1`,
and
verified the portable policy export and terminal manifest. All outputs
used a
one-day lifecycle prefix. The one-turn smoke produced zero reward by
design; it
validates selection, deferred extraction, rollout, training,
checkpointing, and
export rather than model quality.

MarinSkyRL#549 must land first; this change then needs its dependency
pin
updated to the merged commit.

Part of #9122

commits.message:
[tasktrove] Publish clean releases to Hugging Face (#9124)

Publish built TaskTrove releases to a configurable Hugging Face dataset
repository, defaulting to `open-athena/task-trove`. The command streams
release objects into local staging, uploads retained task shards as the
`train` split, keeps the rejection ledger and manifest as downloadable
metadata, and replaces stale Parquet shards on repeat publication. Its
generated dataset card documents provenance, cleanup stages, row and
archive schemas, loading, licensing, and the full release report.

Validate the local release before creating the destination repository.
Clear prior Harbor reward files before every verifier result so an
invalid-task or infrastructure-error rerun cannot expose a stale score.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[tasktrove] Add the TaskTrove conversion pipeline (#9061)

Convert `open-thoughts/TaskTrove` revision `0292300` into Harbor tasks
with an explicit grader contract in `tests/verifier.toml`. The verifier
covers deterministic answers, structured outputs, instruction-following
constraints, repository tests, judge rubrics, and a fail-closed script
fallback. Conversion permits small deterministic repairs and rejects
rows that need answer-recovery heuristics, repository reconstruction,
replacement tests, or a new subjective contract.

Release `2026.09.10.9` processed 1,739,326 input rows and retained
1,449,686 tasks across 43 sources, 19 converters, 12 verifier modes, and
39 Docker environments. The pipeline writes 64 intermediate shards and
one final Parquet file; the final file has 66 row groups and is
3,837,032,177 bytes. Every rejected row is recorded in the release
ledger with its source policy or row-level reason.

The canonical release root is
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/tasktrove/clean/2026.09.10.9/`. It
contains `tasks/part-00000.parquet`, `manifest.json`, `ledger.parquet`,
and `report.md`. Marina serves the cleanup report, source audit, and
paginated Parquet browser at https://marina.oa.dev/tasktrove/ without
exposing object-store credentials.

`tasks/part-00000.parquet` has one retained task per row. Its regular
selector columns are `source`, `family`, `template_id`, `converter`,
`mode`, `dockerfile_id`, `language`, `tags`, and `has_solution`; `path`
is the stable task identifier. The packed payloads are `task_binary` and
optional `solution_binary`. Consumers can select source or family
cohorts from this single canonical object without a second
Hive-partitioned copy.

Historical local-Docker and Daytona studies informed the converters but
do not validate this release byte-for-byte. A later 100-task review of
release `.7` covered every converter, 12 verifier modes, and 23
environments; it escalated 24 rows, then confirmed 17 defects and
cleared seven. Release `.9` applies the narrow confirmed fixes: 11 exact
rows are excluded, one uniformly broken 1,272-row prompt-injection
source is dropped, and two numeric graders regain their stated
tolerances. Suspect and merely weak tasks remain, and no near-dedup pass
was applied.

The `.9` pipeline completed successfully on Iris from clean launch
commit `b76d03131c`; the manifest and sampled generated Dockerfile
record that same verifier ref. After merging current `main`, the
repository test lane passes with 1,794 tests, 4 skips, and 5 expected
failures; TaskTrove's frontend build, four backend tests, lint,
formatting, and type checks pass. Production revision `marina-00055-lkm`
serves image
`sha256:8b549ddaeba89c6548ef38698e461e87ccbd36ffa6c1d5e9aca4b198851ad488`;
an authenticated check confirmed the landing page, `.9` manifest,
exact-source filter, and Parquet-backed row detail.

Part of #9083.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Preserve chat prefixes across content representations (#9067)

Render normalized Harmony conversations with the same template exported
for inference. Keep assistant reasoning, prose, and parallel tool calls
in one turn, emit tool calls inside `<tool_call>` tags, and resolve API
tool reply IDs to function names. Structured tool definitions serialize
as JSON.

Equivalent content represented as strings, text mappings, or lists of
text parts now produces identical text and token prefixes, including
tool replies. Join text parts before trimming so spaces between parts
survive. Stored Datakit text omits BOS because the text tokenizer
supplies it; the trace evaluation path also keeps inline calls in one
assistant turn while retaining separate prose and tool loss labels.

Re-export tokenizer artifacts to deploy the template changes. Keep
vLLM's `chat_template_content_format=string` pin until those artifacts
are deployed. The skipped vLLM Hermes parser test is removed; local
tests cover rendering and token parity, not vLLM parser integration.

Fixes #9103

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[skills] Add the deploy-hero-change playbook (#8873)

Add `.agents/skills/deploy-hero-change/SKILL.md`, the playbook for
swapping the live hero to deploy a significant code change. It encodes
what the 2026-09-02 ragged all-to-all deployment (#8506, #8870) settled
on: agree the handoff checkpoint, run id (`hero-<change>-step<N>k`),
gate, and clock with the user; land the code and the `trigger_hero.sh`
change on main and launch main's script from a pristine worktree with
`--initialize-from-checkpoint` (#8868) so the old run's tree and W&B
history are never written; rehearse fail-closed runbook scripts with an
independent review; compare the new run against the old on the same
batches over 200 steps from a W&B report; and roll back by relaunching
the old commit. It also records the startup costs to expect at hero
shape, why monitoring must read finelog rather than W&B, and the NCCL
RAS plus `iris.task` recipe that localized this deployment's silent hang
to one rack.
